card.summary: No quota of its own. It multiplies the 1TB item limit by however many versions you PUT.

free_tier.stated: No quota of its own. It multiplies the 1TB item limit by however many versions you PUT.

per_object_cap.stated: Guidance, not an enforced cap: a single file in an item should not be larger than ~500 to ~700 GB, with 500 GB the recommended limit.
per_object_cap.notes: The same help page recommends items with fewer than 10,000 files, where the files do not exceed 1TB; the API allows up to 250,000 files.

retention.stated: PUT and DELETE do not keep old versions unless the x-archive-keep-old-version:1 header is sent.
retention.notes: For multipart uploads the header must be specified when the multipart upload is completed..

egress.terms: Free (history files are served through the same item path)

record.tooling: raw IAS3 PUT header; rclone does not expose it, so a thin curl/requests shim is needed
record.chaining: A 20TiB cold archive can be stored as ~20 versions of a 1TB item if the payload changes, or used as a free append-only version store per key. Combined with x-archive-cascade-delete:1 for cleanup.
record.limits_note: For multipart the header must be set at multipart-complete time; each version re-enters the per-item queue.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

record.reliability_note: Unofficial-ish surface: documented but not exposed by any major client, so it is untested at scale and easy to orphan copies with.

evidence.proved: 'For multipart, the x-archive-keep-old-version header must be specified at the time the multipart upload is completed'

evidence.quote: Normally PUT and DELETE do not keep old versions of files around. To have the archive keep old versions of the object you can add the header: `x-archive-keep-old-version:1` Saved versions will be placed in `history/files/$key.~N~`

evidence.proved: the Internet Archive help centre advises a single file stay under about 500 to 700 GB
evidence.quote: A single file in an item should not be larger than ~500 to ~700 GB (capacity depends on activity levels and other circumstances, so we recommend using the lower limit of 500GB).

evidence.proved: files in an item are recommended not to exceed 1TB
evidence.quote: We recommend creating items that have less than 10,000 files, and where the files do not exceed 1TB.

evidence.proved: old versions are kept only when the header is set
evidence.quote: Normally PUT and DELETE do not keep old versions of files around. To have the archive keep old versions of the object you can add the header: `x-archive-keep-old-version:1`

evidence.proved: for multipart the header is set at completion
evidence.quote: (For multipart, the `x-archive-keep-old-version` header must be specified at the time the multipart upload is completed)

record.notes: No quota of its own. It multiplies the 1TB item limit by however many versions you PUT.
